quotes.text: Instead of you moving the data, fabric keeps a live copy of your external database inside one lake, and it refreshes that copy on its own.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines Fabric Mirroring in one sentence as a self-refreshing copy instead of a manual data movement.

quotes.text: One rule is worth memorizing the copy is read only. If something needs to change, you change it in the source system and let mirroring carry the update across.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the key operating rule that keeps a single version of the truth.

quotes.text: If it's locked inside a database that only its own engine can read, expect a copy. If it's already sitting in the open, expect a pointer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a memorable rule of thumb for which mirroring flavor a source gets.

quotes.text: a shortcut points at the part you choose, and mirroring brings in the whole database and lets fabric decide the best way to reach it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Separates shortcuts from mirroring by scope, the most common beginner confusion.

quotes.text: Mirroring needs a running fabric capacity, so if you pause or delete that capacity, mirroring stops and nothing replicates until it comes back.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights the one hard operational dependency to plan around.

takeaways: Fabric Mirroring keeps a continuously updated, read-only copy of an external database in OneLake as Delta tables, without anyone building or maintaining a pipeline.
Shortcuts point at specific open-format data, mirroring brings in a whole database or catalog, and pipelines are for full control over transformations and schedules.
Background replication and mirroring storage are free up to one terabyte per capacity unit, but querying costs normal compute and mirroring stops when the capacity is paused.
hook: Getting operational database data into analytics usually means building and babysitting pipelines. This Simply Explained episode shows data beginners and Fabric newcomers how Fabric Mirroring keeps a near real-time copy in OneLake, how it compares with shortcuts and pipelines, and what it really costs.
